html:
The Timote were a people of the Andes of western Venezuela, in what is now Mérida state. With the Cuica to the north they are called the Timoto-Cuica peoples.

They farmed the high valleys with stone terraces and irrigation, growing maize and potatoes, and kept food in stone lined stores. Their religion had shrines in the mountains and lakes. They were the most advanced farmers of the Venezuelan Andes, though not on the scale of the Muisca to the southwest. Spanish settlers founded Mérida in 1558, and conquest and disease broke up their society. Many rural people of the Mérida Andes descend from them.
sum: The Timote were a people of the Andes of western Venezuela, in what is now Mérida state. With the Cuica to the north they are called the Timoto-Cuica peoples.
